title: PsoChoice - Development of a digital tool to support an individualized, patient-centered selection of systemic therapies for psoriasis vulgaris
summary:
Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin condition for which many different treatments are available. The selection of an appropriate systemic therapy depends on numerous individual factors. These include, among other things, comorbidities, potential risks, previous treatments, as well as patients’ personal preferences and life circumstances. Although medical guidelines provide recommendations for treatment, deciding on a specific therapy in everyday practice is often complex. The goal of this study is to develop and evaluate a digital decision-support system for selecting appropriate systemic therapies for psoriasis. The study aims to investigate whether the system’s recommendations align with the decisions made by experienced dermatologists and whether the recommendations are transparent.
As part of the study, typical treatment scenarios for patients with psoriasis are examined based on responses to a questionnaire. The system developed generates recommendations for possible therapies based on medical guidelines and established decision-making rules. These recommendations are compared with the decisions made by experienced dermatologists. The study focuses exclusively on the decision-making process; patients’ medical treatment is not altered by their participation in the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    Female, male, and non-binary patients > 18 years of age with moderate to severe psoriasis vulgaris
-    Initiation or switch to systemic therapy as part of standard care
-    Ability and willingness to provide written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
-    Inability to give informed consent
-    Participation in another interventional study
